reason: The shared-context pitch actually fits — I run three-plus agents and re-explaining context is a real tax. But I buy on engineering-lead authority and I read every review first; Loom is a new vendor with nothing on Reddit, GitHub, or Twitter vouching for it, and I'm not handing my session data and code to an unknown daemon on launch day. $30/seat is fine; trust isn't there yet.
objection: I don't trust a new vendor with my code and agent session data — no track record, no audit, no one I respect vouching for it, and my first instinct is that it's just another tool to manage.
would_change_my_mind: A third-party security audit, public source or self-host option, or an engineering lead I already trust vouching for it in production.
